title: Black tie optional: what guests should wear
description: What black tie optional means, three safe outfits for women and men, what to wear to a black tie optional wedding, and how it differs from black tie.
sections: Black tie optional vs black tie
Build it from what you own
quick_answer: Dress route: a floor-length gown, or an elevated midi or cocktail dress in a rich fabric. Trouser route: a tuxedo, or a well-fitted dark suit with a tie and polished shoes. Daytime: go one step less formal than you would for an evening event. Skip: anything casual. "Optional" applies to the tuxedo, not to the formality.

title: Cocktail attire: what to wear, with examples
description: What cocktail attire means for women and men, what to wear to a cocktail wedding, day vs evening, and how it differs from semi-formal and formal.
sections: Casual cocktail, business cocktail and festive cocktail
Build it from what you already own
quick_answer: Dress route: a knee- to midi-length dress, a dressy jumpsuit or smart separates in a richer fabric. Trouser route: a suit, usually with a tie, or a tailored blazer with dress trousers. Shoes: heels, polished flats, loafers, oxfords or derbies. Not trainers. Skip: jeans, shorts, flip-flops, and floor-length gowns or tuxedos, which belong to formal and black-tie dress codes.

sections: Try three ways to connect pieces
Check the outfit in your own setting
quick_answer: Easiest: a neutral base (navy, grey, cream, camel, denim) plus one accent colour. Calm: several shades of one colour, with mixed textures. Bold: two opposites on the colour wheel, with one kept small. Twelve ready-made combinations are in the table below .

title: What to wear to a job interview, by industry
description: Interview outfits for every workplace, from finance to start-ups: the dress-one-level-up rule, video interviews and a night-before checklist.
quick_answer: The rule: find out what people wear on a normal day there, then dress one level up. Not sure? Tailored trousers or a skirt, a plain shirt or top, a blazer and polished closed shoes work almost anywhere. Fit beats price: clean, pressed clothes that fit and let you sit comfortably. Video interview: the same top half, solid colours and nothing distracting at the neckline.

title: Play with proportion, keep your comfort
description: Learn how garment lengths, volume and visible layers change an outfit. Try three practical proportion experiments using clothes you already own.
sections: Choose the shape you want today
Make the example fit your day
quick_answer: Decide the shape you want today: roomy, neat or long. Change one thing only: tuck the top, add an open layer or swap the shoe. Walk, sit and reach. Keep the change if it feels good.

title: Turn screen style into everyday outfits
description: Use Blair Waldorf and Rachel Green as starting points. Extract one detail, adapt it to your climate and occasion, and build an outfit of your own.
sections: Rachel: adapt the dress to your climate
quick_answer: Name one detail you love, such as a collar, a colour or an accessory. Match it to your real day: weather, walking and dress code. Build it from clothes you own and leave the rest of the costume behind.

title: Semi-formal attire: what to wear, explained
description: What semi-formal attire means for women and men, what to wear to a semi-formal wedding, day vs evening, and how it compares with cocktail and formal.
sections: Build it from what you own
quick_answer: Dress route: a midi or knee-length dress, a wrap dress, a jumpsuit or a smart trouser suit. Trouser route: a suit in a good fabric; a tie in the evening, sometimes optional by day. Daytime: lighter colours and fabrics. Evening: darker colours and a little more polish. Skip: jeans, trainers, beachwear and floor-length ballgowns.

title: Smart casual for women: 9 outfit formulas
description: What smart casual means for women in the US, UK and Australia, nine outfit formulas from clothes you own, and how it differs from business casual.
sections: What smart casual means, by country
Smart casual for dinner, work and events
quick_answer: The rule: start casual, then add one or two smart pieces. Smart pieces: a blazer, tailored trousers, a crisp shirt, fine knitwear, a midi skirt, loafers or ankle boots. Casual pieces that still work: dark jeans, a clean T-shirt and minimal leather trainers. Skip: gym clothes, beachwear, ripped denim and worn-out shoes.

title: Wedding guest attire by dress code
description: What to wear to a wedding for every dress code, from casual and beach to black tie, for women and men, plus the guest rules on white, weather and culture.
sections: Every dress code at a glance
quick_answer: Find the code: check the invitation and the couple's wedding website. Avoid white and ivory unless the couple asks for it. Match the time: lighter and brighter by day; darker and more polished in the evening. When in doubt, dress up a little and choose shoes for the ground.

title: What to wear in 50–60°F (10–16°C) weather
description: Layering formulas for 50, 55 and 60°F (10, 13 and 16°C) weather, for work, weekends and evenings, with clothes you already own. Fahrenheit and Celsius.
sections: Celsius and Fahrenheit, side by side
quick_answer: Base: a T-shirt, a long-sleeve top or a shirt. Middle: a knit, cardigan or overshirt you can remove. Outer: a light jacket, such as a trench, denim jacket or light wool coat. Bottom and shoes: full-length trousers or a skirt with tights, and closed shoes.

title: What to wear to a funeral: a calm guide
description: What to wear to a funeral, memorial or viewing: colours, outfits for women and men, weather, and how to respect family wishes and religious customs.
sections: Does it have to be black?
Memorial services, viewings and celebrations of life
quick_answer: Colours: dark or muted (black, navy, charcoal, grey, dark green) unless the family asks for something else. Dress route: a simple dress or skirt to around the knee or longer, or tailored trousers with a plain top and a jacket. Trouser route: a dark suit, or dark trousers with a shirt and jacket; a tie is a safe choice. Above all: clean, neat and comfortable enough to stand, sit and walk outdoors.
